standard.title: Classifying Triangles and Polygons
standard.description: classify triangles, quadrilaterals and other polygons according to their side and angle properties; identify and reason about relationships
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have informal familiarity with shape names and basic properties. Students can measure angles and sides.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students classify triangles and quadrilaterals using side and angle properties and reason about hierarchical relationships between shape families.

nodes.label: Classifying triangles by sides and angles
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students classify triangles as scalene, isosceles or equilateral (by sides) and as acute, right-angled or obtuse (by angles), and understand that these classifications are independent.
nodes.minimum_width: Classify a given triangle by both its side and angle properties.
nodes.typical_width: Classify a range of triangles; identify that a triangle can be e.g. isosceles and right-angled simultaneously; investigate which combinations are possible.
wider: Construct triangles with given side lengths and determine which combinations are possible (triangle inequality).
Investigate which combinations of side-type and angle-type are possible vs impossible (e.g. can a triangle be equilateral and obtuse?).

response_modes.reason: Students often treat side classification and angle classification as mutually exclusive. Encountering diverse triangles that require both labels simultaneously resolves this.

success_criteria: Correctly classifies a triangle by both side and angle properties.
Understands that the two classifications are independent.
Does not assume equilateral means right-angled.

nodes.label: Classifying quadrilaterals and their relationships
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students classify quadrilaterals (square, rectangle, rhombus, parallelogram, kite, trapezium) using side and angle properties, and identify hierarchical relationships.
nodes.minimum_width: Classify a given quadrilateral and state the properties used.
nodes.typical_width: Describe, compare and contrast all quadrilateral types; explain hierarchical relationships (e.g. all squares are rectangles, not all rectangles are squares).
wider: Construct a hierarchy diagram (Venn or tree) of quadrilaterals showing subset relationships.
Investigate which quadrilateral properties are necessary vs sufficient for classification.

response_modes.reason: Hierarchical classification requires deliberate reasoning about necessary and sufficient conditions. Students who classify by appearance alone fail with non-standard orientations and confuse the hierarchy.

nodes.hinge_reason: Students who classify by appearance rather than properties cannot design reliable classification algorithms in AC9M7SP04 — the algorithm requires specifying testable property conditions, not visual recognition rules.
success_criteria: Correctly classifies any standard quadrilateral using its properties.
States at least two hierarchical relationships between quadrilateral types.
Does not rely on orientation to classify (e.g. recognises a rotated square).
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Constructing a quadrilateral hierarchy diagram and reasoning about necessary vs sufficient conditions for classification is rich structural thinking — advancing students engage with logic and set relationships within a geometric context.

nodes.label: Classifying other polygons and reasoning about properties
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students classify polygons by number of sides and by regularity, and reason about properties such as line symmetry and convexity.
nodes.minimum_width: Name and classify polygons up to at least octagons; distinguish regular from irregular and convex from concave.
nodes.typical_width: Reason about properties of specific polygons: angle sums, number of diagonals, symmetries.
wider: Investigate tessellation properties: which regular polygons tessellate alone, and why? Connect to interior angles.
Explore polygon properties in architecture, design, and cultural patterns.

response_modes.reason: Classifying polygons draws together side properties, angle sum knowledge, and symmetry reasoning simultaneously.

success_criteria: Correctly classifies polygons by name, regularity, and convexity.
Explains what makes a polygon regular.
Can identify whether a polygon is convex or concave and explain the difference.
